- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after sentiment spikes (high sentiment → high forecast → later correction).
- Forecasts show excessive upward momentum after recent price peaks, failing to account for mean reversion or downward momentum triggered by sentiment cooling.
- When sentiment drops sharply (e.g., 0.12, 0.42, 0.51), model fails to reduce forecast significantly, leading to overcorrection or overshoot in subsequent days.
- Forecasts tend to be overly optimistic in the first 5–7 days of the 30-day horizon, then gradually adjust — but often too late or too much, especially when sentiment is neutral or negative.
- Model underestimates sharp downward moves in late horizon (e.g., 20–30 days) when sentiment is low or trending negative — fails to capture “selloff” or “panic” dynamics.
- Forecast bias is stronger when sentiment is high at the start of the window — model assumes continuation, but reality often shows reversal or consolidation.
- Horizon-specific: 1–5 day forecasts are often too bullish; 25–30 day forecasts are too bearish or flat, especially when sentiment is low or volatile.
- Model does not adequately adjust for sentiment decay — forecasts remain anchored to recent highs even when sentiment is declining.
